chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: The Baltimore laundry
summary: A woman in Baltimore was washing his week of laundry in filthy water, so he took it elsewhere.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: You must have had other problems, like with with laundry. If you're going from one place to the next...

Yes, I had a problem like that once. I remember I put my clothes in to a woman in Baltimore. We had just finished playing Washington. I got a week's worth of dirty clothes. We get into Baltimore, I give it to a woman to wash. Well, we're in Baltimore a whole week! So she don't come by the theatre with the laundry. We're getting ready to leave. And I go by her house to find out if I can get my laundry. This is the last day. So I go upstairs, and I go in the kitchen, and she had 'them in a tub of water -- and you should have seen that water. I said, "Oh, that's all right I just come after my laundry, but I see you're not ready yet." She said, "No, I'm not ready yet." I said, "You can forget it. You should have seen
that water. It looked like she was washin' rubber tires or something in the water. Oh, it was black and greasy...!
